obs: "No man can be bound to do impossibilities. The legislature must be understood to mean that the party should be excused by showing the occurrence of such circumstances as rendered it impossible to perform the condition of the bond."
"if there ever was a case in which the maxim would apply that the law does not oblige to vain or impossible things, we think it is such a one as the present."
"it might well be doubted whether this deed would not retain all the validity it possessed when executed, since its being recorded is rendered impossible by act of law."
The Patapsco Insurance Company v. Southgate
"It was not necessary to issue a subpna. It would have been a useless act."
Cox and Dick v. United States
“It would have been a nugatory act; and the law surely ought not to be so construed as to require of a party a mere idle ceremony.”
Fortier v. New Orleans National Bank

"The law does not and cannot confer upon the lender in such circumstances the power and authority to watch over and control the acts of the married woman who has borrowed money from him, so as to prevent the improper use of the same."
Del Monte Mining & Milling Co. v. Last Chance Mining & Milling Co.

“To say that the subsequent locator must when it appears that his lines are to any extent upon territory covered by a prior valid location go through the form of making a relocation simply works delay …”
Creede & Cripple Creek Mining & Milling Co. v. Uinta Tunnel Mining & Transportation Co.
"it would be a useless and idle ceremony, which the law does not require,"

"If, therefore, we may apply the maxim that the law does not require a vain thing, there is room for the construction that, in vesting in the inspector and engineers the power to determine how wide the barrier pillar should be to secure safety, the intent of the law-making power was to also empower them to say, if such be the fact, that the safety of the men does not require a barrier pillar of any width at all."
Menasha Paper Co. v. Chicago & Northwestern Railway Co.

the court said the railway "was not obliged to do a vain and useless thing..." ... The court, by such holding, counsel says, decided that "the rules must have a reasonable construction." ... counsel insists that ... "the rules must be strictly construed" ... "Rigorously applying the test that the exact letter of the statute must be observed"
H. P. Hood & Sons, Inc. v. United States
"The requirement for finding and proclamation in adopting a base period is not intended to force the Secretary to go through a meaningless-ritual."
National Labor Relations Board v. Dant

"Absent the issuance of a complaint, the filing of a charge is a useless act." ... "Such normal noncompliance at the time of filing a charge should not work to frustrate the *384 Act's purpose of remedying unfair labor practices"
“we should not construe the Act of Congress to require the doing of a useless act.”
Lewis v. National Labor Relations Board
"We cannot read the Act to mean that these burdensome details should be performed by Board members in faraway Washington, D. C."
Tiffany Fine Arts, Inc. v. United States
"In the case of a John Doe summons, where the IRS does not know the identity of the taxpayer under investigation, advance notice to that taxpayer is, of course, not possible."
Kasten v. Saint-Gobain Performance Plastics Corp.
"And it is difficult to see how an employer who does not (or should not) know an employee has made a complaint could discriminate because of that complaint."
